A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, title, core framework and experiments. Their text, equations, figures and complete appendices support a reliable comparison; v4 also includes a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: V2 reports original neural-network experiments, including CIFAR-10 training, representation-alignment measurements and synthetic regression studies in Figures 1–14 and Appendix A.

after.justification: V4 retains these original experiments and their outcomes, including gradient-balance trajectories, representation alignments and sharpness measurements.

M1.justification: The entropic loss in Eq. (3), optimization procedures and network architectures are retained. The revised analytical solutions concern theoretical characterization, without changing a training or inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-10, MNIST, ImageNet and the same synthetic teacher-student and regression scenarios. Appendix A introduces no new dataset, task or evaluation environment.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators, including SGD and Adam in Figures 10 and 12 and the same representation-alignment comparisons. No evaluated comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Appendix A retains the learning rates, batch sizes, training budgets, network widths and alignment measures. The revised analytical sharpness formulas do not document changes to experimental settings or measurement procedures.

E4.justification: The batch-size and weight-decay sensitivity studies, gradient-balance trajectories, entropy-versus-loss analyses and label-noise sharpness experiments are retained. No additional ablation, robustness test or empirical case study appears.

E5.justification: V4's checklist item 7 newly identifies shaded regions as standard errors. V2 already displays these regions and reports five-run averaging in Figures 7 and 9; v4 does not report an increase in runs or new significance testing.

E6.justification: The plotted empirical results in Figures 1–14 are unchanged, as are Appendix A's reported outcomes, including ResNet18 training accuracy of 98% and test accuracy of 88%. The changes to analytical sharpness expressions are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Appendix B.11 substantially revises Theorem 12's singular-value scales to include covariance and embedding factors, explicitly states gamma=0 and eta approaching zero from above, and adds boundary calculations and Lemma 2 with its proof. Theorem 10, Eqs. (16)–(19), and Appendix B.13 revise the sharpness derivation, including replacing V Sigma_x with V sqrt(Sigma_x) in the minimum-sharpness expression.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same main contributions: entropic symmetry breaking, gradient equipartition, universal representation alignment and an explanation of sharpness behavior. The conclusion's added minimum-gradient-fluctuation perspective restates the mechanism already described in Section 3.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 withdraws v2's assertion that minimum sharpness requires both input and label-noise isotropy, including its input-imbalance counterexample. V4 instead concludes that isotropic label noise yields minimum sharpness, materially revising the explanation of which distributional imbalance causes excess sharpness.

D1.justification: The new checklist explicitly identifies PyTorch, states that personal computers suffice, and discloses that an open experimental code/data package is not provided. These are additional disclosures; Appendix A's implementation settings and pretrained-weight access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 49 referenced works and substantive research positioning are retained. V4 repairs unresolved citations to references 6 and 21, which were already in v2's bibliography, without adding literature or changing the novelty claims.

P1.justification: V4 makes localized prose revisions, especially in the sharpness discussion and conclusion, repairs citation rendering and appends a NeurIPS checklist. The existing section sequence and overall narrative remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The document is extensively reformatted into the NeurIPS style, changing typography, text width, title treatment and figure sizing and placement throughout. All 14 figures retain their plotted content and panel structures; the substantial change is their presentation within the new layout.

improvement.justification: V4 addresses important mathematical deficiencies through corrected covariance-dependent solution and sharpness formulas, withdrawal of the input-imbalance counterexample, and explicit derivations supporting the alignment theorem in Appendix B.11. These changes substantially strengthen the accuracy and checkability of two central theoretical applications. Empirical support remains unchanged, while the standard-error disclosure adds limited transparency.
